subject: POC connectivity plan & commitment for API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@mainstreetpharma.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MAP & POC ask — connectivity details

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at MainStreet Pharma thinks Redwood is a strong fit for our clinical documentation summarization POC. We sketched a short mutual action plan internally and attached a draft so we can align on timing and responsibilities. High-level asks from our side for the POC environment: 

- Org setup: we'd like a dedicated tenant (or clear org isolation) so we can lock down roles for our engineers.
- API keys: short-lived service keys for the POC with a single integration key for ingestion services.
- IP allowlist: we'll provide set of static egress IPs for our staging VMs — need an allowlist so tokens are scoped.
- VPC peering: optional but preferred — we want VPC peering to avoid public egress for PHI-containing payloads.

Target timeline: 3-week POC starting as early as Jun 10. Can Redwood commit to environment readiness (org + keys + allowlist) within 7 business days after we sign the MAP?

Attachment: map-draft-v2.pdf (MAP: responsibilities, milestones)
Attachment: vpc-topology.png (internal network sketch)

Thanks —
Alice Nguyen
Director, Data Science
MainStreet Pharma
alice@mainstreetpharma.com
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@mainstreetpharma.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP & POC ask — connectivity details

Alice — really appreciate the clear ask and attachments. We're excited to partner on this POC. Quick confirmation of next steps from Redwood's side: 

1) Org & tenant: we will provision a dedicated org for MainStreet within our staging cluster and add your two invited admin users (please share emails).
2) API keys: we'll generate a scoped service key for ingestion and a short-lived developer key. Keys will be created with default rate limits and can be rotated on your request.
3) IP allowlist: send your egress CIDRs and we'll apply them to the tenant's network policy.
4) VPC peering: ops needs your VPC CIDR and AWS account ID to generate the peering proposal; peering approval is typically 24-48 hours once we have route tables.

We can aim for the 7-business-day readiness you requested if contracts and the MAP are signed by Wed 5/30. Marissa (CS) I'll hand this to you for ops scheduling; Neha, could you confirm whether our standard peering flow (route-based, cross-account) works for them?

Proposed immediate action:
- Alice: share admin emails + egress CIDRs + AWS account ID by EOD 5/26.
- Marissa: schedule provisioning slot the week of 6/3.
- Neha: confirm technical peering checklist and any additional network constraints.

I'll sync with legal on the MAP redline separately.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Lead, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
From: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP & POC ask — connectivity details

Rafael / Marissa — copying a quick checklist for ops so we don't miss anything. I'm pasting Alice's ask below for reference.

Quoted message:
> From: Alice Nguyen <alice@mainstreetpharma.com>
> High-level asks from our side for the POC environment:
> - Org setup: dedicated tenant
> - API keys: short-lived service keys
> - IP allowlist: static egress IPs
> - VPC peering: optional but preferred

Technical checklist (items for Redwood ops):
- Tenant provisioning: create org-id MSP-POC-2028, pre-seed two admin users (emails to be provided).
- Key policies: create two key scopes: ingestion.readwrite (service), dev.read (dev key) + TTL 30d for service key; document rotation endpoints.
- IP allowlist: apply customer CIDRs at tenant network policy; whitelist only management/control plane endpoints by default.
- Peering flow: request customer's AWS account ID, VPC ID, and intended route table IDs. We'll provision a VPC peering connection request (us-east-1).
- Security/compliance: enable audit logging for the tenant (30d retention) and ensure no persistent logs contain raw PHI.

Risks / blockers:
- If customer requires HSM-protected keys or custom KMS, that's an extra step (needs Product/Infra approval) — flag early.
- If their staging egress uses ephemeral IPs (NAT autoscaling), we'll need a static egress layer or proxy.

Marissa — suggest a 30-min runbook review with customer's infra lead and our ops engineer on Mon 5/29. I can lead the peering checklist walk-through.

-Neha

neha_kapoor
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
